target: Bydd y plant yn perfformio yn nrama'r ysgol.
english: The children will perform in the school play.
tip: The word yn meaning in triggers nasal mutation: drama becomes nrama in yn nrama'r ysgol (in the school play).

target: Os bydd hi'n bwrw glaw, bydda i'n dal y bws.
english: If it rains, I'll take the bus.
tip: To rain is bwrw glaw, literally throw rain: Os bydd hi'n bwrw glaw = if it rains.

target: Os bydd yr athro'n absennol, bydd y wers yn cael ei chanslo.
english: If the teacher is absent, the lesson will be cancelled.
tip: Welsh builds the passive with cael plus ei: bydd y wers yn cael ei chanslo = the lesson will be cancelled.

target: Mae Math fab Mathonwy yn hudol.
english: Math son of Mathonwy is magical.
tip: In old names son of is fab, a mutation of mab: Math fab Mathonwy = Math son of Mathonwy.

target: Cefais i gyfarfod cynhyrchiol gyda fy niwtor.
english: I had a productive meeting with my tutor.
tip: my (fy) triggers nasal mutation on the next word: fy niwtor = my tutor.

target: Os bydd amser gyda fi, bydda i'n paentio'r ffens.
english: If I have time, I'll paint the fence.
tip: Welsh shows having with gyda, not a verb: amser gyda fi = time with me, meaning I have time.

target: Mae gan Gymru hunaniaeth genedlaethol gref sydd wedi'i gwreiddio yn ei hiaith, ei diwylliant a'i hanes.
english: Wales has a strong national identity that is rooted in its language, culture and history.
tip: Another way to say has is Mae gan: Mae gan Gymru hunaniaeth = Wales has an identity.

target: Basai'r plant wrth eu bodd.
english: The children would be delighted.
tip: wrth eu bodd means delighted, literally at their pleasure. The possessive tracks the subject, so the children take eu, their.

target: Nhw oedd wedi codi'r arian.
english: It was they who raised the money.
tip: Fronting the pronoun adds emphasis: Nhw oedd means it was them who did it, stronger than a plain they had.

target: Dywedodd hi y basai'n well ganddi de.
english: She said she would prefer tea.
tip: Welsh has no verb for prefer. It uses gwell gan, better with someone: well ganddi de means she prefers tea.

target: Bydd hi'n ymweld â'i rhieni'r penwythnos nesaf.
english: She will visit her parents next weekend.
tip: ymweld, to visit, takes â (with) before its object: ymweld â'i rhieni, visit her parents, never a direct object.

target: Bydda i'n dod â'r pwdin i'r parti.
english: I will bring the dessert to the party.
tip: To say bring, Welsh uses dod â, literally come with: dod â'r pwdin means bring the dessert.

target: Bydd e'n gorffen y prosiect erbyn dydd Gwener.
english: He will finish the project by Friday.
tip: erbyn means by, as in by a deadline something must be done: erbyn dydd Gwener, by Friday.

target: Os cloi di'r drws, bydd y tŷ'n ddiogel.
english: If you lock the door, the house will be safe.
tip: After os (if), Welsh uses a short verb for the future: cloi di means if you lock, no separate word for will.

target: Dw i wedi bod yn sâl ers deuddydd nawr.
english: I've been ill for two days now.
tip: For a duration still going on, use ers with a perfect: wedi bod yn sâl ers deuddydd, have been ill for two days.

target: Oni bai am y glaw, basen ni wedi mynd.
english: But for the rain, we would have gone.
tip: Oni bai am means but for, or if it weren't for: Oni bai am y glaw sets up an unreal cause, the rain that did happen.

target: Dywedodd y pennaeth fod yr ysgol yn cau'n gynnar.
english: The headteacher said the school was closing early.
tip: In reported speech, that is fod, from bod: Dywedodd... fod yr ysgol, said that the school, links the two clauses.

target: Pe baen ni'n byw'n agosach, bydden ni'n ymweld yn amlach.
english: If we lived closer, we would visit more often.
tip: Pe baen ni means if we, marking an unreal or hypothetical if rather than a likely one: Pe baen ni'n byw, if we lived.

target: Cod dy galon, bydd pethau'n gwella.
english: Keep your chin up, things will improve.
tip: Cod dy galon literally means lift your heart, the everyday Welsh for chin up or take heart.

target: Carwn i eich gwahodd i'r digwyddiad.
english: I would like to invite you to the event.
tip: Carwn i is a polite I would like, the conditional of caru: Carwn i eich gwahodd, I would like to invite you.

target: Byddan nhw'n symud i Gaerfyrddin y mis nesaf.
english: They will move to Carmarthen next month.
tip: The position word i (to) softens the next consonant, so Caerfyrddin becomes i Gaerfyrddin, c turning to g.

target: Os ca i'r swydd, bydda i'n symud i Gaerdydd.
english: If I get the job, I'll move to Cardiff.
tip: ca i is the short future of the irregular cael, to get: os ca i'r swydd means if I get the job.

target: Yn sicr, bydd y prosiect yn cael ei gwblhau erbyn yr haf.
english: Certainly, the project will be completed by summer.
tip: Welsh forms the passive with cael plus a possessive: cael ei gwblhau, literally get its completing, means be completed.

target: Fe yw'r aelod hynaf o'r tîm.
english: He is the oldest member of the team.
tip: hynaf means oldest, the superlative of hen, old. Welsh superlatives usually end in -af.

target: Mae'n dal i'w weld a fydd y diwygiadau'n cyflawni eu hamcanion.
english: It remains to be seen whether the reforms will achieve their goals.
tip: For an indirect yes-or-no question, whether is a: a fydd y diwygiadau, whether the reforms will.

target: Baswn i'n plannu blodau.
english: I'd plant flowers.
tip: Baswn i'n means I would. The 'n links Baswn i to the verb: Baswn i'n plannu = I would plant.

target: Basai fe'n costio gormod.
english: It would cost too much.
tip: Basai is the he or it would form; Baswn is I would. Basai fe'n costio = it would cost.

target: Addawodd e y byddai'n dod.
english: He promised he would come.
tip: For reported would, use y byddai (that he would): Addawodd e y byddai'n dod = he promised he would come.

target: Ni oedd wedi paratoi'r bwyd.
english: It was us who prepared the food.
tip: Front the doer for emphasis: Ni oedd wedi paratoi = it was us who prepared, literally we were who prepared.

target: Taswn i yn dy le di.
english: If I were in your place.
tip: Taswn i means if I were, the informal conditional: Taswn i yn dy le di = if I were in your place.
